title: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and ver
question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.

prediction.sql:
WITH step_scores AS (
  SELECT name, version, step,
         MAX(CASE WHEN model = 'Stack' THEN test_score END) AS stack_score,
         MAX(CASE WHEN model <> 'Stack' THEN test_score END) AS max_nonstack
  FROM model_score
  GROUP BY name, version, step
),
model_status AS (
  SELECT m.name, m.version, m.L1_model,
         CASE
           WHEN EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM step_scores s
             WHERE s.name = m.name AND s.version = m.version AND s.step = m.step
               AND s.stack_score IS NOT NULL AND s.max_nonstack IS NOT NULL
               AND s.max_nonstack < s.stack_score
           ) THEN 'strong'
           WHEN EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM step_scores s
             WHERE s.name = m.name AND s.version = m.version AND s.step = m.step
               AND s.stack_score IS NOT NULL AND s.max_nonstack IS NOT NULL
               AND s.max_nonstack = s.stack_score
           ) THEN 'soft'
         END AS status
  FROM model m
),
counts AS (
  SELECT status, L1_model, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM model_status
  WHERE status IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY status, L1_model
)
SELECT status, L1_model, cnt
FROM counts c
WHERE cnt = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM counts c2 WHERE c2.status = c.status)
ORDER BY status, cnt DESC, L1_model;

base_solution_anchor.base_sql:
WITH step_scores AS (
  SELECT name, version, step,
         MAX(CASE WHEN model='Stack' THEN test_score END) AS stack_score,
         MAX(CASE WHEN model<>'Stack' THEN test_score END) AS max_nonstack
  FROM model_score
  GROUP BY name, version, step
),
model_status AS (
  SELECT m.name, m.version, m.L1_model,
         CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN s.stack_score > s.max_nonstack THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'strong'
              WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN s.stack_score = s.max_nonstack THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'soft'
         END AS status
  FROM model m
  JOIN step_scores s ON m.name=s.name AND m.version=s.version AND m.step=s.step
  GROUP BY m.name, m.version, m.L1_model
),
counts AS (
  SELECT status, L1_model, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM model_status
  WHERE status IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY status, L1_model
)
SELECT status, L1_model, cnt
FROM counts c
WHERE cnt = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM counts c2 WHERE c2.status=c.status)
ORDER BY status, cnt DESC, L1_model;

persistent_recovery_advisory_draft.base_sql:
WITH stack_scores AS (
  SELECT name, version, step, test_score AS stack_score
  FROM model_score
  WHERE model = 'Stack'
),
nonstack_max AS (
  SELECT name, version, step, MAX(test_score) AS max_nonstack
  FROM model_score
  WHERE model <> 'Stack'
  GROUP BY name, version, step
),
status AS (
  SELECT s.name, s.version, s.step,
    CASE
      WHEN n.max_nonstack < s.stack_score THEN 'strong'
      WHEN n.max_nonstack = s.stack_score THEN 'soft'
    END AS status
  FROM stack_scores s
  JOIN nonstack_max n
    ON s.name = n.name AND s.version = n.version AND s.step = n.step
),
l1 AS (
  SELECT st.status, m.L1_model
  FROM status st
  JOIN model m
    ON st.name = m.name AND st.version = m.version AND st.step = m.step
  WHERE st.status IS NOT NULL
),
counts AS (
  SELECT status, L1_model, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM l1
  GROUP BY status, L1_model
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT status, L1_model, cnt,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY cnt DESC, L1_model) AS rn
  FROM counts
)
SELECT status, L1_model, cnt
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY status;
